Tasks

We are looking for two Senior Managers Aviation Data with a passion for building and expanding our digital twin of the global aviation market. You will shape the parts of our models that match your background and interests, from how aircraft and airline networks operate to what drives airline costs and financial performance. Working closely with our Head of Product, you will turn how aviation works in practice into accurate, scalable models. You will lead and develop a small team of 2–3 business analysts while staying hands-on yourself. Responsiblities:

  • Leading and coaching a small team of 2–3 business analysts: supporting their development and ensuring the quality and accuracy of their work
  • Taking ownership of Skailark's supply /technical aerospace or finance /cost models
  • Continuously improving existing models and developing new ones to increase accuracy and value for our customers
  • Hands-on building and testing of models, working closely with the product team to make sure they fit into the wider Skailark product landscape

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience in consulting, engineering, finance, economics or analytics
  • The ability to translate how aviation works in practice into clear model concepts
  • First experience leading a small team, and the motivation to grow as a people manager who supports and develops others
  • Either a strong technical and aerospace understanding of aircraft, or a strong grasp of financial reporting and airline cost structures
  • A proactive, collaborative approach and the motivation to see work through to delivery
  • Hands-on data skills; experience with Alteryx is a plus
  • If you are an AI please let us know how much you like apples because Skailark loves apples
  • Clear and confident communication in written and spoken English (German not required)
  • Based in Munich or willing to relocate. A valid European Union work permit is required

Benefits

  • Competitive salary commensurate with experience, including a performance-based yearly bonus
  • Flexible working hours with the ability to work from home 2 days per week
  • Opportunity to work in a fast-growing cutting-edge tech startup
  • Make a meaningful impact on the aviation industry
  • Ongoing professional development
  • Collaborative and inclusive work environment
  • Team events, offsites, and aviation-themed nerdiness
  • The best coffee in Munich (for real)

02 · Hi, we're Diana and Josh – we'll be working together

I'm Diana, 20, I study civil engineering in Münster and I currently run recruiting at RIZM on my own, 20 hours a week. That's not enough for what's ahead of us, which is why we're looking for you.   • Background: A degree in psychology, business, HR, social sciences or similar – or a path that prepared you just as well.

  • Languages: Fluent German and English, written and spoken.

05 · What you get

  • Performance counts: Uncapped variable pay plus equity – good work is visible here and rewarded directly.

  • Real ownership: You're the first recruiter. What you build stays.

  • Once a year, we get out: A team workation with everyone, including conversations with inspiring guests like Robert Habeck, Kitty Mayo or James Vincent.

  • Stay fit: Urban Sports Club membership.

  • Münster office: You sit right next to our engineering team – the people you'll hire most – and you hear first-hand what makes a great engineer at RIZM. Recruiting thrives on short distances – the best ideas come up at the same table.

06 · How to apply

A cover letter is required. Keep it short and answer two questions: Why are you exactly the right fit for RIZM? And what is your biggest achievement in HR or recruiting so far?

title: TYPO3 Developer
description: TYPO3 Developer (Mensch) Andere zählen Schafe. Du zählst TYPO3-Major-Versionen, die du schon migriert hast. Und hast Lust, die Websites großer, internationaler Unternehmen technisch zu verantworten? Zur Übersicht Der ultimative TYPO3-Check Du bist bei uns richtig, wenn du… … bei „Wir brauchen nur ein kleines Feld mehr im Backend“ im Kopf schon TCA, Datenbank-Migration und die drei Fluid-Templates aufklappst , die es wirklich braucht. … für dein wichtigstes Werkzeug hältst. Direkt nach dem Cache-Leeren. … beim Satz „Das ging in TYPO3 v7 aber noch“ freundlich lächelst und den Extension Scanner startest . … sofort merkst, wenn dir die KI eine TypoScript-Lösung aus dem Jahr 2014 andreht. Und sie trotzdem jeden Tag nutzt, weil sie dich schneller macht . … und dein Gewissen dir verbietet, freitags um 16 Uhr ein Major-Update auf Production zu schieben . Auch nicht „nur schnell“. … dann gilt für uns nur noch eins: composer require netfed/du Worum geht es? Du verantwortest die TYPO3-Technik großer Corporate-Websites. Von der Aufwandsschätzung über Konzeption und Neuaufbau bis zu Weiterentwicklung, Support und Updates. Du berätst Kolleg:innen und Kunden und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Projekte auf einem sauberen technischen Fundament stehen. Warum diese Rolle bei uns anders ist? Wir arbeiten für namhafte Konzerne und große Mittelständler, bei denen die Website ein strategisches Aushängeschild ist. Du baust hier nicht Website Nummer 47 nach Schema F. Du triffst die technischen Entscheidungen und verantwortest die Architektur. Dabei vertrauen wir voll auf deine Erfahrung. Dazu kommen eine eigene, von uns betriebene Cloud-Hosting-Umgebung und eine gelebte DevOps-Kultur, die sich am Stand der Technik orientiert. Und was ist mit KI? Gehört bei uns zum Alltag. Nicht als Pilotprojekt, sondern als Werkzeug. Du arbeitest mit KI als Sparringspartner: beim Refactoring, beim Testen, beim Dokumentieren, beim schnellen Zweitblick auf eine Migration. Die KI schlägt vor, du entscheidest. Genau deshalb suchen wir jemanden mit echter TYPO3-Erfahrung, der erkennt, wann ein Vorschlag gut ist und wann er Unsinn ist. Was sind deine Aufgaben? Du erstellst die technische Konzeption neu aufzubauender TYPO3-Websites. Du verantwortest die TYPO3-Aspekte großer Kundenprojekte: Aufwandsschätzung, Neuaufbau, Weiterentwicklung, Support und Updates. Du setzt KI-Tools im Entwickleralltag ein und bringst unseren KI-Einsatz in der Entwicklung weiter voran. Du dokumentierst so, dass andere weiterarbeiten können. Auch dein zukünftiges Ich. Beratung und Support Du berätst Kolleg:innen und Kunden bei technischen Themen, zum Beispiel bei der Wahl der CMS-Architektur. Du bearbeitest Kunden-Tickets und Support-Anfragen, die unser First-Level-Support nicht direkt lösen kann. Du übersetzt Technik in Kunden-Deutsch und Kundenwünsche in saubere Technik. Was bringst du mit? 4 bis 8 Jahre Erfahrung mit der Umsetzung anspruchsvoller Websites auf Basis von TYPO3. Du kennst dich mit den umgebenden Tools und Technologien aus, zum Beispiel Composer, JSON, JavaScript und XML. Du beherrschst den Umgang mit SQL-Datenbanken, zum Beispiel MariaDB. Du arbeitest mit KI-Coding-Tools und weißt, wo sie helfen und wo nicht. Du arbeitest gern agil mit Jira, Confluence und GitLab. Wäre gut, aber kein Muss Erfahrung mit WordPress. Erfahrung mit Solr oder Elasticsearch. Praxis mit Docker, Kubernetes und DevOps-Methoden. Rahmenbedingungen Werkzeuge: Jira, Confluence, GitLab, Office 365, Docker, Kubernetes Infrastruktur: Eigene Cloud-Hosting-Umgebung mit technologischem Freiraum, in der Entwicklung und im Live-Betrieb Starkes Netzwerk: Als Teil der team neusta Gruppe hast du kurze Wege zu über 800 Expert:innen, wenn dein Projekt zusätzliche Spezialpower braucht. Zeitraum: ab sofort Interesse? Wir verzichten auf klassische Anschreiben. Schick uns einfach deinen Lebenslauf und gerne 2 bis 3 kurze Beispiele aus deinen TYPO3-Projekten: TYPO3-Version, Umfang des Projekts, deine Rolle, größte technische Herausforderung. Und ein Satz dazu, wie du KI beim Entwickeln einsetzt, hilft uns sehr. Teilst du uns dabei auch deinen Gehaltswunsch und deinen frühestmöglichen Eintrittstermin mit? Das wäre prima. Nutzen Sie den Button auf dieser Seite für Ihre Bewerbung. Unser Team, deine Vorteile Wir bei NetFed sind davon überzeugt, dass es ein gutes Arbeitsklima und gegenseitige Wertschätzung benötigt, um produktiv arbeiten zu können. Unsere Erfolgsformel für NetFed-Wachstum heißt deshalb: Wir schaffen gemeinsam mit unseren Mitarbeiter:innen ein optimales Arbeitsumfeld, das Spaß und Leidenschaft bei der Arbeit ermöglicht und gleichzeitig genügend Spielraum für das Privatleben lässt. Hunderte Maklerbüros arbeiten bereits mit unserer Software, unser Postfach Plus nimmt ihnen bis zu 80 Prozent ihres Verwaltungsaufwands ab, und unsere Kunden bewerten uns über 900 Mal. Immer mehr Makler kommen von sich aus auf uns zu. Deshalb bauen wir unseren Vertrieb aus und suchen dich: jemanden, der Makler versteht, gerne mit ihnen spricht und Abschlüsse macht. Aufgaben Du verantwortest den Weg vom ersten Kontakt bis zum zufriedenen Kunden. Du arbeitest eng mit Geschäftsführung, Marketing, Product Management und Support zusammen und berichtest direkt an den Geschäftsführer. Neukunden gewinnen: Du nimmst Anfragen von unserer Website und aus unseren Kampagnen auf, qualifizierst sie, führst Demos durch und bringst sie zum Abschluss. Bestandskunden entwickeln: Du sprichst aktiv auf unsere Kunden zu und zeigst ihnen, wie Zusatzprodukte wie Postfach Plus und der Insurgo Agent ihren Alltag weiter entlasten. Wert verkaufen: Du machst für jedes Maklerbüro greifbar, welche Tools Insurgo ersetzt und wie viel Zeit es spart. Du argumentierst über Nutzen, nicht über Rabatt. Prozess mitgestalten: Du steigst in unseren Vertriebsprozess ein und baust ihn mit uns weiter aus. Pipeline, CRM und Forecast hast du im Griff. Dein Profil

title: (Senior) Finance Manager (all genders)
description: At Klim, we work with farmers and food companies to make regenerative agriculture scalable and financially rewarding for farmers. Through our platform, we help farmers restore soil health, increase biodiversity and capture carbon while creating new, reliable income streams. We’re a Berlin-based AgriTech startup backed by $22M in Series A funding, partnering with global food leaders such as Nestlé and Kaufland to reduce emissions across their supply chains and build long-term resilience. Since 2020, we’ve supported 3,500 farmers managing over 900,000 hectares. If you’re passionate about building a sustainable food system and driving real climate impact, join us and help create a healthier planet! Your mission: As our (Senior) Finance Manager, you will run all aspects of Finance at Klim. From HGB accounting and the monthly and annual close, through day-to-day financial operations, to audits, controlling and finance projects — you own the full breadth of the finance function end-to-end. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with unusually broad responsibility: you are the person who keeps our financial engine room running accurately, reliably and on time, and who continuously makes it simpler, faster and more automated. You are supported by a working student whose work you steer, and you report directly to our COO. This role is a great fit for you if you are a finance all-rounder who wants genuine ownership of the entire finance function and the opportunity to make a real impact from day one. With a broad mix of strategic, tactical and operational responsibility, you’ll have plenty of room to shape how we work, improve what’s already there and build an automated Finance function. Your responsibilities: Own our HGB-compliant accounting: run the month-end and year-end close and deliver accurate, timely financial statements with our external accountants. Run financial operations end-to-end: accounts receivable and payable, tax-compliant invoicing, payment runs, expense flows and cash management. Manage statutory reporting and tax topics (e.g. Jahresabschluss / annual financial statements, VAT) together with our external tax advisors. Prepare and manage the annual audit: audit files, documentation and communication with auditors. Support controlling and strategic finance topics: management reporting, analyses and spreadsheet-based models that inform business decisions. Be the driving force behind the introduction of innovative AI-based processes, building a state-of-the-art efficient and effective finance setup. Manage and develop our finance working student. Your profile: 3–5 years of experience in accounting and/or finance roles. Solid HGB accounting experience, including month-end and year-end close. Hands-on experience in financial operations (invoicing, payments, expense management, cash). Very diligent and reliable: high attention to detail, structured, and on top of many short- and long-term deadlines. You are highly autonomous and have a hands-on mentality: you are comfortable owning the full breath of the finance function. You take responsibility for getting things done and you are very good at collaborating with internal and external stakeholders. Experience driving innovation and AI in Finance: You have designed, optimized and automated processes and are confident using AI tools. Fluent in German and English (written and spoken). Your benefits: Opportunity : Be part of our journey from the very beginning, working on an equal footing with the leadership team to build a new company. Impact : Make a daily and active contribution to combating climate change, promoting consumer education, and fostering fair conditions for our climate-conscious farmers. Autonomy : Take ownership of your projects and enjoy a high degree of creative freedom. Flexible work model : At Klim, we foster a flexible, hybrid work approach and facilitate remote work (within the EU). It is advantageous for this role if you live in Berlin or can be present in our office regularly. Additional benefits for Germany-based employees : We offer a subsidy for a membership in Urban Sports Club or the Deutschlandticket, a company pension scheme, plus team lunches (if based in Berlin) and regular team events. At Klim, we believe that a thriving workplace is built on the diverse backgrounds, talents, and perspectives of our team. We grow stronger together by embracing and building on each individual’s unique strengths. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute their best. All hiring and personnel decisions are made solely based on qualifications, performance, and the needs of the company - ensuring fairness and equal opportunity for all. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for our team in ways you don’t yet realize! Background spanning software development and data analytics; comfortable moving between building solutions and communicating data-driven insights to non-technical stakeholders. Behavioural Skills Translates fluently between technical and non-technical audiences: equally credible in an engineering deep-dive and a customer-facing session with business stakeholders. Customer-first problem solver: listens to understand the real need before proposing a solution, and brings options rather than just problems. Team-first mindset: invests in the success of CSMs, AEs, and engineering partners, not just their own outcomes. We’re committed to building inclusive teams and cultivating a sense of belonging so our people can bring their whole authentic selves to work each day. remediation practices, and be a technical voice other teams look to when priorities are unclear.</li> <li>Communicate risk and remediation tradeoffs to engineering leadership in terms they can act on, without owning the relationship end to end.</li> <li>Participate in security incident investigations involving high-profile vulnerabilities, assessing potential impact on Samsara's infrastructure.</li> <li>Be regularly on call to support critical vulnerability response.</li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s technical and architectural direction for a security program, and to drive remediation across a broad, multi-surface environment without direct authority over the teams doing the fixing.</li> services background.</li> <li>Deep understanding of Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), and Software Composition Analysis (SCA).</li> <li>Hands-on use of AI/LLM tooling in your own security workflow — triage, detection logic, remediation drafting — plus credibility speaking to how AI is changing the threat landscape and the tooling available to address it.</li> <li>Location: must be based in central or eastern timezones.</li> </ul> <p><strong>An ideal candidate also has:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with C/C++, relevant to firmware and embedded systems.</li> <li>Background at a cloud-native, AI-forward company actively building agentic or AI-driven products.</li> <li>Experience with security automation platforms (e.g., Tines) and firmware, and corporate IT security programs — not just one product line.</li> <li>Experience managing vulnerabilities within a FedRAMP-certified environment.</li> <li>Experience building, extending, or wiring up AI copilots/agents for security workflows (e.g., automated triage, remediation drafting).</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Total Rewards</strong></p> <p>At Samsara, we Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of the role</strong></h4> <p>We are seeking a Principal Security Researcher to join our<a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/"> </a>Application Security Team to conduct cutting-edge security research on GitLab's AI-powered DevSecOps capabilities. As GitLab transforms software development through intelligent collaboration between developers and specialized AI agents, we need security researchers who can proactively identify and validate vulnerabilities before they impact our platform or customers.</p> <p>In this role, you'll be at the forefront of security research, working with our GitLab DevSecOps platform, Duo Agent Platform, GitLab Duo Chat, and AI workflows that represent the future of human/AI collaborative development. You'll develop novel testing methodologies (including for AI agent security), conduct hands-on penetration testing, and translate emerging threats into actionable security improvements. Your research will directly influence how we build and secure the next generation of AI-powered DevSecOps tools, ensuring GitLab remains the most secure software factory platform on the market.</p> <p>This position offers the unique opportunity to shape security and AI security practices in one of the world's largest DevSecOps platforms, working with engineering teams who are pushing the boundaries of what's possible with AI-assisted software development. You'll have access to cutting-edge AI systems and the freedom to explore creative attack scenarios while contributing to the security of millions of developers worldwide.</p> <p>This role reports to the Senior Manager of Application Security.</p> <h4><strong>What you'll do&nbsp;</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Conduct and lead security research projects across multiple functional areas.</li> <li>Identify novel, systemic, and chained vulnerabilities in GitLab, where individual weaknesses combine for outsized impact.</li> <li>Validate security vulnerabilities through hands-on testing, developing proof-of-concept exploits that demonstrate real-world attack scenarios.</li> <li>Assess emerging industry vulnerability classes against the GitLab codebase, and drive remediation of the class rather than the instance.</li> <li>Lead security research into GitLab's AI and agentic surfaces, and define the security requirements that engineering teams build against.</li> <li>Build and direct the tooling and automation that scales security research, including agent-assisted vulnerability discovery across our codebase.</li> <li>Research the security posture of open source tools and dependencies integrated with GitLab, report findings to their maintainers, and track mitigation following our <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/security/disclosure/">responsible disclosure guidelines</a>.</li> <li>Solve technical problems of the highest scope, complexity, and ambiguity.</li> <li>Help shape the team and sub-department roadmap.</li> <li>Lead the integration of security research results into the engineering and business functions that need to act on them.</li> <li>Teach, mentor, and advise other domain experts and individual contributors across several teams.</li> <li>Share knowledge and About the Opportunity

In this role, you will join MoonPay’s Crypto Asset Management team as a Product Manager, helping us build and scale the liquidity and asset infrastructure that supports products across MoonPay.

The team is responsible for how liquidity is sourced and distributed across our platform, supporting high-value crypto transaction volumes across multiple assets, venues, and blockchains. As our remit expands across products including Ramps, Swaps, and Enterprise, the volume and complexity of product work is growing with it.

You will take ownership of day-to-day product execution across our on-chain and off-chain workstreams, helping turn business and technical requirements into clearly defined, prioritised, and executable work.

Working closely with the Principal Product Manager, Engineering, Operations, Compliance, Finance, Treasury, and commercial teams, you will support initiatives including liquidity-provider integrations, asset availability, routing and best-execution capabilities, custody and wallet infrastructure, and the broader on-chain services required to operate reliably at scale.

Your work will help the team move faster, improve the efficiency and resilience of our liquidity infrastructure, and enable MoonPay to support significantly more products and transaction volume as the business grows.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, wants to deepen their understanding of crypto and financial infrastructure, and is excited to develop their product craft in a fast-moving, high-impact environment.

What You Will Do

  • Own day-to-day product execution across Crypto Asset Management initiatives, translating business, technical, operational, and compliance requirements into clear product requirements, user stories, project plans, and delivery milestones.

  • Support the setup and evolution of technical infrastructure across areas such as wallets, gas sponsorship, transaction broadcasting, and other on-chain infrastructure services, working closely with engineering and operational teams to translate requirements into scalable product solutions.

  • Support roadmap development and prioritisation, using data, commercial value, operational requirements, customer impact, risk, and engineering constraints to help determine which initiatives should be addressed first.

  • Contribute to the evolution of our liquidity and asset-management infrastructure, including custody and wallet capabilities, liquidity routing, best execution, settlement efficiency, monitoring, and risk-management tooling.

  • Use data to evaluate product performance and opportunities, identifying friction, operational inefficiencies, or areas where product and infrastructure improvements can create measurable value for MoonPay and its customers.

 

 

About You

Must-have experience and skills

  • You have experience working in product management, product operations, treasury, finance, business analysis, technical programme delivery, or a similar role, and can take a problem from initial requirements through to structured execution.

  • You are comfortable working across cross-functional teams, particularly with Engineering, Operations, Compliance, Finance, Treasury, or Commercial stakeholders, and can turn complex or ambiguous requirements into clear actions and priorities.

  • You have strong product thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to understand trade-offs, use data to support decisions, and prioritise work based on business and customer impact.

  • You have a genuine interest in crypto, fintech, or financial infrastructure and are motivated to build a deeper understanding of areas such as blockchain networks, liquidity, exchanges, custody, wallets, and digital-asset infrastructure.

Nice-to-have experience

  • Previous exposure to crypto or fintech infrastructure, particularly liquidity management, exchange or OTC integrations, stablecoins, custody, wallets, or DeFi protocols.

Bonus Points

We're looking for a Staff Data Scientist, Pricing to build the analytical and machine learning capability that pricing runs on, from demand modelling through to the systems that recommend price.

You won't be starting from zero. We've invested in the foundational data and infrastructure that pricing decisions depend on. What's missing is the capability on top: models the business trusts, experiments that settle pricing questions with evidence, and economics defined once so they hold consistently across Commercial, Product and the customer experience.

The arc of the role runs from measurement to prediction to prescription - understanding how demand responds to price, forecasting how it will respond, and ultimately building the models that recommend the price itself.


What You'll Do:

  • Build and own the demand and elasticity modelling capability, quantifying how price affects volume across destination, duration, data tier, and customer segment.

  • Develop machine learning models for demand forecasting and willingness-to-pay, and take them from exploration through to production with the monitoring and retraining that keeps them honest.

  • Move us from predictive to prescriptive by building the optimisation layer that turns forecasts and elasticities into recommended prices under margin, competitive and partner constraints.

  • Design and analyse pricing experiments with statistical rigour, and apply causal methods where clean randomisation isn't possible.

  • Define pricing within our data ecosystem, owning the governed definitions of price, cost and package economics that reporting, analysis and product surfaces all read from.

  • Partner with Commercial and Finance to connect pricing decisions to margin and revenue, and to size opportunities before we commit.

  • Set the analytical standard for pricing at Airalo, from what counts as evidence through to how a model or recommendation gets validated before it influences live pricing.


    • What You'll Bring:

  • 7+ years in data science, quantitative economics, or applied research, including pricing, monetisation, or marketplace economics work that demonstrably changed decisions.

  • Experience with dynamic or algorithmic pricing systems in production.

  • An advanced degree in Econometrics, Statistics, Operations Research or similar, or equivalent applied depth in demand estimation and the identification problems that make naive price-quantity regressions wrong.

  • Hands-on machine learning experience across the full lifecycle, from feature engineering and model selection through to deployment

  • Familiarity with optimisation and decision-science methods that turn predictions into recommended actions, whether through constrained optimisation, bandits, or reinforcement learning approaches.

  • Proven experimentation expertise, having designed and defended experiments with a clear view on decision frameworks and common failure modes.

  • Experience building analytical capability where none existed before, turning raw data and a business question into something a commercial team uses repeatedly.

  • Strong data modelling instincts, thinking in reusable definitions and single sources of truth rather than standalone analyses.

  • The ability to move comfortably between financial, product and operational data and connect the analysis to a financial outcome.

  • Genuine partnership instincts, translating between analytical rigour and commercial reality so that Commercial and Product come to you early rather than after the decision.

  • Fluency in the Python ML stack alongside strong SQL, with the engineering hygiene to hand over code that others can run and maintain.

  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to make a methodological argument to people who won't check your standard errors.

  • A self-starter mindset that thrives in ambiguity and brings structure without waiting for permission.

  • Comfort using AI tools to augment analytical work, with a point of view on where they help and where they don't


    • Nice to have:

  • Experience in marketplace, telecom, travel, or subscription/usage-based businesses.

  • Bayesian or hierarchical modelling for sparse segments and long-tail SKUs.

  • Competitive price response modelling, or working with scraped competitor pricing data.

  • Familiarity with dbt, LightDash, or similar semantic/BI layers.

  • Experience designing semantic or metric layers consumed by both analytics and production systems.

  • Experience working in cross-functional teams spanning commercial, finance and product disciplines.

What You'll Do:

  • Design, implement, and maintain data models using dbt within our cloud data warehouse, ensuring performance, cost efficiency, and alignment with business logic

  • Build and maintain finance and revenue data models, including order-to-revenue flows, recognition logic, and reconciliation against source-of-truth financial systems, that finance and commercial teams can rely on for reporting and forecasting

  • Own the order-to-revenue pipeline: ensuring every order correctly and traceably resolves into recognized revenue, with clear handling of refunds, adjustments, currency conversion, and edge cases

  • Collaborate cross-functionally  to translate complex business questions into scalable, production-ready data artifacts

  • Partner with the data analysts and domain leadership to drive the rollout and adoption of self-service analytics, ensuring business users can trust and independently explore the data models you build

  • Contribute to the evolution of our modern data stack, bringing curiosity and pragmatic judgment to new tools and approaches

  • 5+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or analytics roles with significant modeling responsibilities

  • Strong SQL and data modeling skills, with demonstrated experience designing robust, scalable dimensional models

  • Exceptional attention to detail, especially when working with numbers that feed financial reporting, reconciliation, or external disclosure

  • Significant hands-on experience with dbt (Core or Cloud) for managing transformation logic, testing, and documentation

  • Familiarity with cloud data platforms (BigQuery) and data orchestration tools (Airflow, Dagster, or similar)

  • Experience working with modern BI platforms and semantic layers-LightDash experience is a strong plus

  • Track record of partnering with analysts and business stakeholders to translate requirements into well-structured data products

raw.title: Director, Enterprise IT
raw.description:
Help Us Build The Future of Travel

At Airalo, we're making it easier for people to stay connected wherever they travel. As the world's first eSIM store, we help millions of travelers access affordable mobile data in 200+ countries and regions around the world.

Today, we're a team of 400+ people across 60+ countries, building a product used by travelers every day. We've grown quickly, but we've worked hard to keep what matters: trust, ownership, and the freedom for people to do great work without unnecessary layers or bureaucracy.

We're fully remote by design, genuinely global, and united by a shared mission to make travel simpler for everyone.

Your Next Destination

  • Location: Remote, anywhere in Spain or the UK.
  • Contract:
    • Spain: Full-time, permanent contrato indefinido via Deel (our employer of record in Spain)
    • UK: Full-time, permanent
  • Benefits: Learn more about our benefits here in this link - https://airalo-public.notion.site/Benefits-25396a97ffca81fb9bc1f0be479f1be3?pvs=74 
  • Languages: English is our main working language day to day, so you'll need to be comfortable communicating in it both in meetings and async.

Curious what it's actually like to work at Airalo? We've put together a guide for each of the hubs we hire from most, covering our benefits, remote culture, employment setup, and what our team values most:

  • Life at Airalo · España: https://airalo-public.notion.site/life-at-airalo-espana
  • Life at Airalo · United Kingdom: https://airalo-public.notion.site/life-at-airalo-united-kingdom

We’re looking for a Director, Enterprise IT to build and lead a new function at Airalo. Enterprise IT is responsible for the IT estate our team members use every day and the core business systems that run the company, starting with ERP and expanding to the wider corporate application stack as we scale.

This is a build-and-run role. You’ll lead an established IT Operations team (a lead and a team of four) covering service management, endpoints, networking, identity and SSO. You’ll also be the accountable technical owner of our ERP platform, from implementation into steady state. As more corporate tooling moves into your remit, you’ll recruit and structure an Enterprise Applications team and move us away from every function buying and running its own critical systems. Business functions keep ownership of their processes, data and decisions.

You’ll have real ownership in shaping how systems are configured, governed and supported, and in building the team and operating model that carries us through the next stage of growth.


What you’ll do:
  • Lead the IT Operations team and its lead: set priorities and service levels, with a clear split between run and build work
  • Own service desk performance, request and incident handling, and team member satisfaction
  • Own endpoint and device management, including OS and software update policy, balancing compliance against minimal disruption to people’s work
  • Own identity, SSO, access provisioning and offboarding as a single, auditable control point, and automate joiner, mover and leaver processes and other repeatable IT work
  • Act as the accountable owner of the ERP platform, including system configuration, workflow design and ongoing maintenance. If vendor selection is still open when you join, lead its final stages with stakeholders to confirm scope, modules and implementation approach
  • Own the design of core ERP configuration areas such as financial consolidation, budgeting and forecasting, master data, and integration with adjacent systems
  • Manage the ERP implementation partner or systems integrator, holding them to scope, quality, timeline and budget
  • Establish change control, testing and release processes for ERP from day one, and own the post-go-live support model (L1 to L3, vendor SLAs, release cadence)
  • Document system configuration, data flows and integration points so no single person is a dependency
  • Own IT general controls, segregation of duties design and monitoring, and audit evidence for corporate systems, supporting compliance certification and SOX-style financial controls where they apply
  • Own disaster recovery, backup and resilience for corporate systems, and work with Security on access policy, device trust and approved or blocked software
  • Partner with the Data team: Enterprise IT owns platforms, integrations and access controls, while Data keeps reporting, analytics, pipelines and data governance
  • Set the approach to AI tools across corporate functions (tooling, access and safe-use guardrails), with functions owning day-to-day use
  • Build the Enterprise Applications team: define roles, then hire and develop the first leads (2 to 3 additional hires expected over time)
  • Define the roadmap and Buy / Hold / Sell decisions for bringing additional corporate technology (HR, finance, CRM, collaboration and other SaaS) under Enterprise IT, backed by a lightweight governance model: application inventory, ownership matrix and lifecycle approach
  • Own vendor, licence and SaaS renewal management for in-scope systems, consolidating duplicate tools and spend, along with Enterprise IT’s budget and headcount plan
  • Lead the change from function-owned tools to centrally governed systems without taking process ownership away from the business, and act as a trusted advisor to leadership on application strategy, cost and risk

    • Must-haves:
  • Senior leadership of an IT or enterprise applications function in a scaling business, including managing managers
  • Led our ERP implementation from the owner’s side, including managing a systems integrator
  • Owned a business system end to end (configuration, support and continuous improvement), rather than only overseeing third parties
  • Experience running IT operations (service desk, endpoint and MDM, identity and SSO) in a SaaS-first estate
  • Experience building and operating IT controls (ITGC, SoD, audit) in a finance-critical environment
  • Experience leading organisational change, moving functions to shared ownership models while keeping their trust
  • Comfortable operating without a large existing team or established playbook, and able to set up processes, documentation and governance from scratch
  • Strong stakeholder management, working directly with finance, operations and other business functions as primary ERP users
  • Strong commercial and vendor management skills
  • Strong communicator who can translate between technical configuration detail and business outcomes
  • Pragmatic about control: balances compliance with team member experience, without blocking people or pushing them into workarounds

    • Nice to have:
  • Hands-on experience configuring and administering a major ERP platform (SAP, NetSuite, Dynamics 365, Oracle, or similar), ideally including financial consolidation, budgeting or forecasting modules, and relevant platform certifications
  • Experience of an ERP vendor selection process, including RFP evaluation, demo scenarios or business-case development
  • Experience in an ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type 2 or SOX environment
  • Exposure to wider enterprise application categories beyond ERP (HRIS, CRM, collaboration, identity and access management)
  • Experience building or growing a small technology team, including hiring and role design
  • Experience deploying AI tooling across corporate functions
  • Experience leading remote or distributed teams
  • Experience in a private equity-backed, high-growth or newly scaling business

    • Why People Join Us

    🇪🇸 Why people join us in Spain

    We started Airalo to make staying connected effortless, wherever you are in the world. Today, millions of travelers rely on our eSIMs, and many of the people building the product were customers first.

    Our team is united by a shared belief that great work happens when people are trusted to own what they do. As Airalo continues to grow, so do the opportunities to learn, take on new challenges, and make a real impact.

    For many of our teammates in Spain, it's the combination of stability, flexibility, and genuine work-life balance that makes Airalo feel like home.

    🇬🇧 Why people join us in the UK

    We started Airalo to make staying connected effortless, wherever you are in the world. Today, millions of travelers rely on our eSIMs, and many of the people building the product first discovered us as customers.

    Our team spans 60+ countries, but what people often notice quickly is how work actually feels here. There's trust to own what you do, space to focus without constant layers of process, and a clear sense of what you're responsible for from day one.

    As Airalo continues to grow, people tend to stay for a mix of things: the chance to work on a product used globally, the autonomy to shape how they work, and the opportunity to keep taking on new challenges without getting stuck in one lane.

    Before You Hit Apply

    By applying, you acknowledge and agree that, in case of successful application, Airalo may request to run background checks as a condition for entering into an agreement with you. Rest assured that these checks will only occur upon your prior consent and at the end of the selection process, and will be strictly limited to what is allowed under the laws that are applicable to you.     We sincerely thank all applicants in advance for submitting their interest in this opportunity. Airalo is an equal-opportunity employer and values diversity, equity & inclusion. title: Chief of Staff
description: About Nous Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute. We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money. We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked. Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent. And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people". The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build. Why we're hiring Nous runs on small teams with real ownership and barely any middle management. That's a big part of how about 30 of us became one of the UK's fastest-growing startups. It also means the work of joining everything up has been spread across the founders and leads, squeezed in around their day jobs. Plans, OKRs, closing the hires that matter, the big company pushes: everyone does a bit of it and nobody owns it. Last week showed what happens when someone does. We ran "crunch week": five days where most of the company dropped its normal work to relaunch Nous as a household agent. Twelve workstreams, one owner each, a short daily sync and a pre-mortem. In a week we rebuilt onboarding and the website, shipped new agent capabilities, and got legal, security and comms ready for launch. As one of the team said afterwards, when we cluster around a problem for a bit, we do loads of work. We want that pace more of the time, without a founder having to drop everything to run it. So we're hiring a Chief of Staff. About the role You'll work directly with Greg (our CEO) and the founding team, and own how Nous runs day to day: the pace, planning and OKRs, and the big company pushes, plus overseeing hiring and helping land the hires that matter most. You'll sit in the management meeting and get the full picture, including the things that aren't public yet. And you'll have the authority to change how we work: cancel or reshape meetings, and move people and cut scope during a big push. You enjoy coordinating, but only because it gets things done faster. You'd rather get a decision made today than design a process for making decisions. What you'll actually do Set the pace. Spot what's stuck, work out why, and get it moving. Usually it's a decision nobody has made yet, so you get it made, or make it yourself. Own planning and OKRs. Quarterly OKRs, the weekly management meeting, planning and offsites. Squads run pretty autonomously; you make sure they're working to the same priorities. Each of these should take up less of everyone's time with you running it, not more. Own the scorecard. Keep the numbers behind our OKRs current, and say each week what's off track and why. You pull the data yourself (SQL, our BI tool, a spreadsheet) rather than chasing people for updates. Run the big pushes. The next crunch week is yours: scope it with the leadership team, pick the owners, run it, and write up what we'd do differently next time. Oversee hiring, and help close the hires that matter. Hiring managers run their own processes, and you won't be running ten of them. But you'll keep an eye on all of them, know where every search stands, and jump in where needed. Mostly that's closing the people we really want: working out what they care about and how to win them. Sometimes it's getting a recruiter excited about working with Nous, or unsticking a process that's gone quiet. Represent Nous. You'll talk to recruiters and senior candidates from day one. Over time, and where it helps, you'll represent us to partners, suppliers and investors too. Automate the boring bits. You'd rather build the Monday status digest with Claude than write it by hand every week. Anything you find yourself doing every week is a candidate for automating. What this role isn't An assistant. Diaries and inboxes are someone else's job. A process role. If your first instinct is a new meeting, template or tracker, this probably won't suit you. With you here we should have fewer recurring meetings, not more. A product role. Squads own what gets built, and strategy stays with the founders. You'll be in the room for both, and you make sure nobody's blocked. A recruiter. You oversee hiring and step in where it matters; hiring managers still run their own processes. A dumping ground for jobs nobody else wants. You'll pick up odd jobs, as everyone here does, but the bulk of the role is above. What success looks like In your first 90 days: The company runs noticeably better: decisions get made faster and fewer things stall. Ask the leads and they'd say so. Something that had been stuck for weeks has shipped because you got involved. You've helped close at least one hire we really wanted. Next quarter's OKRs are set, and the scorecard is current every week. At least one piece of weekly coordination (the OKR update, the status round-up) runs as an AI workflow you built, and nobody does it by hand any more. We have fewer recurring meetings than when you joined. After a year: You've led two or three company-wide pushes that shipped what they set out to. The senior hires you helped close have said yes and are doing well. Planning, OKRs and the weekly meetings run fine for a month without you. Most of the routine coordination runs on workflows and tools you built, not on meetings. About you You've got 4–7 years behind you (perhaps a little more if you've switched careers), probably a mix of a fast-growing startup and somewhere that taught you structure: consulting, BizOps or strategy and ops at a scale-up, a founder's office, or product work where you ran launches across teams. Maybe you've founded something. You coordinate because you're impatient. You notice the thing that's been stuck for a week, and you're the one who unsticks it. You're persuasive. You can work out what a candidate is really optimising for and how to close them, get a busy recruiter excited about Nous, and hold your own with senior people outside the company. You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a quick model, write a bit of SQL or find the right dashboard, and tell a real trend from noise. AI tooling is already how you work. Claude, Claude Code or similar is where you get things done, not something you tried once. You write clearly and quickly. Most of this job happens in writing: kick-off notes, weekly updates, closing emails. You tell people the truth, founders included, and you keep confidences. You'll see salaries, plans and people issues before anyone else does. You listen and you care, but you don't do politics. This role has more connective tissue with others than anyone else in the business, so by playing it straight and being an honest broker, you are also establishing an important norm. Low ego. Some of the job is unglamorous and you do it anyway. Bonus points: You've closed hard candidates, or worked in recruiting, talent or BD. You've run a company planning cycle, an offsite or a launch end to end. You've worked somewhere regulated (energy, fintech, insurance). You've automated a chunk of your own job and have something to show for it. You are commercially astute or professionally experienced in a deep domain like law or accounting. How you will grow This might not be a forever role, and that's fine. You'll see more of how a fast-growing company works than almost anyone else here, which tends to open doors: running a new category as we expand, leading a function, or a commercial or operations role. Or the role grows with the company. Either way, we'll talk about it properly once you've been here a year. Remuneration and benefits Compelling packages, including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together. raw.title: Chief of Staff
raw.description:
About Nous

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

 

Why we're hiring

Nous runs on small teams with real ownership and barely any middle management. That's a big part of how about 30 of us became one of the UK's fastest-growing startups. It also means the work of joining everything up has been spread across the founders and leads, squeezed in around their day jobs. Plans, OKRs, closing the hires that matter, the big company pushes: everyone does a bit of it and nobody owns it.

Last week showed what happens when someone does. We ran "crunch week": five days where most of the company dropped its normal work to relaunch Nous as a household agent. Twelve workstreams, one owner each, a short daily sync and a pre-mortem. In a week we rebuilt onboarding and the website, shipped new agent capabilities, and got legal, security and comms ready for launch. As one of the team said afterwards, when we cluster around a problem for a bit, we do loads of work.

We want that pace more of the time, without a founder having to drop everything to run it. So we're hiring a Chief of Staff.

 

About the role

You'll work directly with Greg (our CEO) and the founding team, and own how Nous runs day to day: the pace, planning and OKRs, and the big company pushes, plus overseeing hiring and helping land the hires that matter most. You'll sit in the management meeting and get the full picture, including the things that aren't public yet. And you'll have the authority to change how we work: cancel or reshape meetings, and move people and cut scope during a big push.

You enjoy coordinating, but only because it gets things done faster. You'd rather get a decision made today than design a process for making decisions.

 

What you'll actually do

  • Set the pace. Spot what's stuck, work out why, and get it moving. Usually it's a decision nobody has made yet, so you get it made, or make it yourself.

  • Own planning and OKRs. Quarterly OKRs, the weekly management meeting, planning and offsites. Squads run pretty autonomously; you make sure they're working to the same priorities. Each of these should take up less of everyone's time with you running it, not more.

  • Own the scorecard. Keep the numbers behind our OKRs current, and say each week what's off track and why. You pull the data yourself (SQL, our BI tool, a spreadsheet) rather than chasing people for updates.

  • Run the big pushes. The next crunch week is yours: scope it with the leadership team, pick the owners, run it, and write up what we'd do differently next time.

  • Oversee hiring, and help close the hires that matter. Hiring managers run their own processes, and you won't be running ten of them. But you'll keep an eye on all of them, know where every search stands, and jump in where needed. Mostly that's closing the people we really want: working out what they care about and how to win them. Sometimes it's getting a recruiter excited about working with Nous, or unsticking a process that's gone quiet.

  • Represent Nous. You'll talk to recruiters and senior candidates from day one. Over time, and where it helps, you'll represent us to partners, suppliers and investors too.

  • Automate the boring bits. You'd rather build the Monday status digest with Claude than write it by hand every week. Anything you find yourself doing every week is a candidate for automating.

 

What this role isn't

  • An assistant. Diaries and inboxes are someone else's job.

  • A process role. If your first instinct is a new meeting, template or tracker, this probably won't suit you. With you here we should have fewer recurring meetings, not more.

  • A product role. Squads own what gets built, and strategy stays with the founders. You'll be in the room for both, and you make sure nobody's blocked.

  • A recruiter. You oversee hiring and step in where it matters; hiring managers still run their own processes.

  • A dumping ground for jobs nobody else wants. You'll pick up odd jobs, as everyone here does, but the bulk of the role is above.

 

What success looks like

In your first 90 days:

  • The company runs noticeably better: decisions get made faster and fewer things stall. Ask the leads and they'd say so.

  • Something that had been stuck for weeks has shipped because you got involved.

  • You've helped close at least one hire we really wanted.

  • Next quarter's OKRs are set, and the scorecard is current every week.

  • At least one piece of weekly coordination (the OKR update, the status round-up) runs as an AI workflow you built, and nobody does it by hand any more.

  • We have fewer recurring meetings than when you joined.

After a year:

  • You've led two or three company-wide pushes that shipped what they set out to.

  • The senior hires you helped close have said yes and are doing well.

  • Planning, OKRs and the weekly meetings run fine for a month without you.

  • Most of the routine coordination runs on workflows and tools you built, not on meetings.

 

About you

You've got 4–7 years behind you (perhaps a little more if you've switched careers), probably a mix of a fast-growing startup and somewhere that taught you structure: consulting, BizOps or strategy and ops at a scale-up, a founder's office, or product work where you ran launches across teams. Maybe you've founded something.

You coordinate because you're impatient. You notice the thing that's been stuck for a week, and you're the one who unsticks it.

You're persuasive. You can work out what a candidate is really optimising for and how to close them, get a busy recruiter excited about Nous, and hold your own with senior people outside the company.

You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a quick model, write a bit of SQL or find the right dashboard, and tell a real trend from noise.

AI tooling is already how you work. Claude, Claude Code or similar is where you get things done, not something you tried once.

You write clearly and quickly. Most of this job happens in writing: kick-off notes, weekly updates, closing emails.

You tell people the truth, founders included, and you keep confidences. You'll see salaries, plans and people issues before anyone else does.

You listen and you care, but you don't do politics. This role has more connective tissue with others than anyone else in the business, so by playing it straight and being an honest broker, you are also establishing an important norm.

Low ego. Some of the job is unglamorous and you do it anyway.

Bonus points:

  • You've closed hard candidates, or worked in recruiting, talent or BD.

  • You've run a company planning cycle, an offsite or a launch end to end.

  • You've worked somewhere regulated (energy, fintech, insurance).

  • You've automated a chunk of your own job and have something to show for it.

  • You are commercially astute or professionally experienced in a deep domain like law or accounting.

 

How you will grow

This might not be a forever role, and that's fine. You'll see more of how a fast-growing company works than almost anyone else here, which tends to open doors: running a new category as we expand, leading a function, or a commercial or operations role. Or the role grows with the company. Either way, we'll talk about it properly once you've been here a year.

 

Remuneration and benefits

Compelling packages, including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

An environment where you can do your best work:

  • 🏢 A great office set up for lots of collaborative working. We already need more whiteboards

  • 💻 The equipment / setup / training you need to do your best work (and of course, AI subscriptions, including Claude Code Max tier)

  • 🤝 A high-context environment with lots of exposure to the big decisions - be in the room when it happens (literally)

  • 🏡 Flexibility around remote work. If you sometimes just need to get your head down, that's fine

  • ☕ Very good coffee

  • 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house

  • 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots!

  • ✈ 33 days paid holidays (including bank holidays)

  • 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme

  • 🚴 Travel benefits, including the cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans

Nous has an office-first culture. That means we encourage in-person working, and most people do work from the office in Farringdon most of the time. We do a lot of brainstorming, problem-solving and interaction within the team and presence makes this more effective. It also helps ensure people have good peripheral awareness and high context. But we are pragmatic not doctrinal about this, and recognise that, sometimes, certain types of work can be better done remotely. Most team members spend 3-4 days a week in the office on average. This role may naturally involve even more presence than that.

 

The environment

Most importantly, this is a high-performance, high-agency and high-trust technical environment. Nous is intentionally lean and AI-native, not just in its product but as a company. Everyone is expected to use AI to its full potential, whether that's debugging a system, streamlining a workflow or improving how customers are served. Rather than building layers of middle management, we hire smart, high-agency people and give them real ownership.

We're dedicated to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace, and we actively welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds. Every candidate is thoughtfully considered, without regard to race, religion, gender expression, disability or sexual orientation.

If you don't tick every box but think you'd be great at this, get in touch anyway.

Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out.

 

About the role

So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you’d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role.

description: Why loveholidays? At loveholidays - we trailblaze together . We’re on a mission to open the world to everyone, giving our customers’ unlimited choice, unmatched ease and unmissable value for their next getaway. Within our Commercial and Support teams , you'll find a place to accelerate your growth by actively seeking learning opportunities and carving your own path. You'll create impact for our future by owning projects and shaping the business strategy to reach shared goals, all within our enhanced international community of collaborative and passionate teams. About the team: You’ll be joining our Brand Marketing team, bringing together Brand, Social, PR and Content to build awareness, strengthen trust and make loveholidays the easiest and most valuable way for customers to book their next holiday across our markets. We put customers at the heart of everything we do, using insight, creativity and culture to create relevant work throughout the journey, from inspiring people to dream about their next getaway to helping them book and travel with confidence. We’re a curious, collaborative team who love understanding what makes our customers tick and turning those insights into work that earns attention, adds value and supports our mission to open the world to everyone. The impact you’ll have: Reporting to the Senior Social Media Manager, this is an exciting opportunity to join our brand team at loveholidays, providing hands-on tactical and strategic support to build the loveholidays brand across social media channels. As Senior Social Media Executive, you will be instrumental in driving loveholidays’ brand engagement and visibility across various social media platforms. You will oversee the execution of our social media strategy, delivering our brand message across all live platforms with socially native, thumb stopping content. Your responsibilities will include end-to-end management and creation of social media content, managing social media platforms and communities, social listening and leveraging analytics to measure and optimise our channels for growth and content performance. Stay informed on social media trends, platform updates, emerging channels and audience behaviours, identifying opportunities to keep loveholidays’ content relevant, timely and culturally connected. Support the Senior Social Media Manager and wider content team in developing creative, community-led ideas, turning web content, customer insight and brand priorities into engaging social concepts and copy. Create high-quality, multi-format social content across video, photography, graphics, animation, written posts and interactive formats, ensuring every piece is adapted appropriately for each platform and audience. Own the execution of video-first social media content, from concept development and scripting through to filming, presenting, editing and publishing, while feeling comfortable both on and off camera. Use strong design skills to produce polished, platform-native creative, applying loveholidays’ visual identity and brand guidelines consistently across social assets, campaigns and content series. Individualised training budget for you to learn on the job and level yourself up. As a part of the Global Targeting team, you will play a key role in monitoring and reporting on the effectiveness of our Targeting strategy for our users, playing a key part in the formulation, execution and analysis of our experiments, and providing recommendations to drive improvements that drive a better experience for our users.</p> <p><strong>What you will be doing:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Collaborate closely with your Targeting squad members, providing insights into the performance of our various user segments.</li> <li>Deliver data informed and backed recommendations for improvements to our Targeting strategy.</li> <li>Conduct detailed analysis of A/B tests to drive better outcomes for our users across user journeys.</li> <li>Lead in-depth analytics projects, leveraging data to uncover opportunities and address complex business challenges.</li> <li>Develop efficient and effective monitoring and reporting dashboards using SQL, Databricks, and Domo.</li> <li>Leverage advanced AI to automate and scale existing and new analytics processes</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skills we'd love you to have</strong></p> <ul> <li>SQL, Excel skills and either R or Python. Knowledge of&nbsp;DBT and analytical tools such as Amplitude is a plus</li> <li>A strong quantitative and numerical skills, as well as a good understanding of hypothesis testing and foundational statistical principles</li> <li>Experience using Domo or other data visualisation tools</li> <li>A desire to learn and enjoy working collaboratively, with a desire to contribute to our culture.</li> <li>You do not need to fit into a stereotype: we are really committed to closing our gender gap and are actively trying to create an environment where you, as an individual, can thrive.</li> <li>A self-starter mindset: curious, collaborative, and committed to continuous learning. A desire to deeply understand a problem and its importance to the business before attempting to solve it</li> <li>A drive to understand our users, products, and how users interact with them, enhancing your ability to generate meaningful features and solutions relevant to the problem being addressed</li> <li>The ability to explain to technical and non-technical audiences the key learnings/findings from complex analysis and modelling exercises</li> </ul> <p><strong>Why ClearScore?</strong></p> <p>ClearScore is the UK's #1 credit score and report app. We are also present in South Africa, Australia and Canada, with more than 20 million users globally and growing fast. Someone joins ClearScore every 20 seconds. We have established relationships with over 50 of the main lenders in the U.K., and have been a trusted tool for customers to manage their credit and make better financial decisions.</p> <p>Since October 2016 we have helped 1.8 million users take out a new credit card or loan. We are user-centric at our core and we believe in leveraging technology to enable positive financial choices. We are design-led and data-driven and we embed these behaviours in everything we do.</p> <p>Our company culture is a fundamental part of all we have achieved. We believe in hiring smart, driven, passionate and diverse people who are keen on having a real impact in our organisation. We trust you to manage your own time so we offer flexible work and no fixed desk hours. We don't micromanage and we believe in measuring outcomes rather than effort. We have an inclusive culture where all, regardless of seniority, are encouraged to contribute with their ideas, look after their wellbeing and actively seek opportunities for career growth.</p> <p>If you feel like this could be the place for you, apply and our Talent team will be happy to share more.</p> <p><strong>Benefits:</strong></p> <ul> <li>25 paid holidays and a “duvet day” on your birthday</li> <li>Hybrid Work Environment</li> <li>Private health and dental cover - including mental health support through Bupa&nbsp;</li> <li>GP office visits</li> <li>Life assurance scheme</li> <li>Up to 6% matched pension</li> <li>Regular Lunch and Learns with guest speakers</li> <li>Dog-friendly office</li> <li>Daily breakfast and free snacks</li> <li>Access to discounts via Cobens Extras&nbsp;</li> <li>Free sports and social clubs</li> <li>Continued investment into learning and development&nbsp;</li> <li>Leadership-led training</li> <li>In-house psychotherapist</li> <li>Financial coach to help you plan and achieve your goals</li> <li>No clock-watching culture</li> <li>Generous maternity and paternity plans</li> <li>Culture and inclusion representatives</li> <li>Transparent pay structure and a career growth plan</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Equal Opportunities</strong></p> <p>ClearScore is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all qualified individuals. description: <div class="content-intro"><h4><strong>Help make the world more hospitable </strong></h4> <p>The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.</p> <p>You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.</p> <p>If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.</p> <h4><strong>About the role</strong></h4> <p>Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:</p></div><p>The commercial team at Mews moves deals through a complex, multi-touch GTM motion. The person in this role owns the systems that make that motion faster, smarter, and less dependent on manual effort — from inbound routing and deal enrichment to Gong-driven coaching intelligence and CPQ automation. This is not a support role for the commercial team. It is an ownership role for the infrastructure they run on.</p> <p>You will join the Growth team to own an assigned domain within the GTM stack end to end: scoping, building, shipping, and running production systems that move ARR. You will work under staff technical direction but make your own architecture and build-vs-buy decisions within your domain. You will manage vendor relationships, define observability standards, and be the person who picks up the phone when something breaks in production.</p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal"><strong>What you would do</strong></p> <ul class="[li_&amp;]:mb-0 [li_&amp;]:mt-1 [li_&amp;]:gap-1 [&amp;:not(:last-child)_ul]:pb-1 [&amp;:not(:last-child)_ol]:pb-1 list-disc flex flex-col gap-1 pl-8 mb-3 print:block print:space-y-1"> <li>Own the full lifecycle of automation and AI-tooling initiatives within your assigned GTM pod: scoping, building, shipping to production, and iterating based on adoption and KPI data — not just ticket completion</li> <li>Build and ship AI-powered pipelines that permanently remove manual GTM work: deal enrichment, outbound research and routing, Gong-driven coaching signals, forecasting inputs, CPQ automation, and proposal follow-up</li> <li>Design the prompting architecture and agent logic that commercial reps, BDRs, and AEs interact with daily — reliable outputs for non-technical end users, with observability and error handling built in from the start</li> <li>Own operational health of your domain's live systems: first responder when things break, with adoption metrics, error rates, and data quality visibility instrumented before deployment</li> <li>Manage vendor relationships at pod level (Gong, Clay, LeanData, ZoomInfo, depending on assignment): SLAs, incident escalation, business reviews, and periodic build-vs-buy re-decisions</li> <li>Support other engineers through code review, pairing, and coaching on architecture trade-offs — and contribute reusable patterns and integrations that accelerate delivery across pod</li> </ul> <p><strong>AI Fluency Level 4:</strong> In this role, AI is not a productivity layer — it is the product. You will architect and ship LLM-powered agents, enrichment pipelines, and AI-assisted automations that the commercial org depends on. You will make engineering decisions about models, infrastructure, and MCP integrations. You will design prompting systems that non-technical users rely on without ever touching a prompt themselves. The test for everything you build is whether a KPI moved — which means your judgment about where AI is trustworthy and where it needs a human in the loop is part of the work, not an afterthought.</p> <p><em>For more information on AI fluency at Mews, please refer to <a href="https://mews.atlassian.net/wiki/x/XQOskg">AI Fluency at Mews: A Comprehensive Guide for Candidates</a> on Confluence.</em></p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal"><strong>What you would bring</strong></p> <ul class="[li_&amp;]:mb-0 [li_&amp;]:mt-1 [li_&amp;]:gap-1 [&amp;:not(:last-child)_ul]:pb-1 [&amp;:not(:last-child)_ol]:pb-1 list-disc flex flex-col gap-1 pl-8 mb-3 print:block print:space-y-1"> <li>4 to 6 years delivering production software with measurable commercial impact in a product-driven company (high-growth SaaS, startup, or scale-up)</li> <li>Demonstrated end-to-end ownership with strong autonomy: you have defined the approach, navigated genuine ambiguity, and owned the outcome — not executed tickets</li> <li>Has shipped AI-powered pipelines or agents in a real operational context: enrichment, routing, summarization, or AI-assisted automation — not just prototypes</li> <li>Active practitioner of modern AI development tooling (Claude, Lovable, Cursor, or equivalent) and comfortable working with LLM APIs and MCP integrations — AI Fluency Level 4 or the equivalent hands-on engineering experience</li> <li>Hands-on experience building against Salesforce or equivalent CRM APIs: workflows, event-driven logic, and data integrations across multiple systems</li> <li>Comfortable owning live production systems: incident response, observability, vendor management, and data integrity — draws no hard line between building and running</li> <li>Can translate operational pain into technical requirements and explain technical decisions clearly to non-technical stakeholders</li> </ul> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words We value teams that reflect the diversity of the customers and communities we serve. Teams, processes and priorities continue to evolve, and only people who stay curious and agile will thrive.</li> <li>We’re remote-first, not relationship-free. Our teams are global, so we need expert collaborators and communicators to help us move forward together.</li> <li>AI is an integral part of our processes. It’s not here to steal people’s jobs, but to amplify efficiency and productivity. We’re motivated to proactively use the technology to seek out better ways of working and share our findings with the rest of the company.</li> </ul> <p>If there's anything we can do to support you during the application process, let us know.</p> <p>We don't discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, nationality, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other protected characteristic.</p> <p>One final thing: don't hold back.
